title: Security review for XSS
when: The user asks for a security review of web code, or the app shows user supplied or fetched text on the page.
inputs: where user or external data enters
prompt:
Goal: No path lets untrusted text become markup or script, with each sink found and replaced by a safe API.
Steps:
1. List data sources: form fields, URL params and hash, localStorage, fetched JSON, file contents, postMessage.
2. Search the sinks: innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval, new Function, setTimeout with a string, href or src set from data.
3. Render text with textContent or createElement plus append; set attributes with setAttribute on an allowlist.
4. For URLs from data, parse with new URL() and allow only http, https or mailto protocols to block javascript: links.
5. Remove inline event handlers and inline scripts so a Content Security Policy can block injected ones.
6. On servers, escape HTML when building pages from data (& < > " ' to entities) and set the response Content-Type.
Quality bar:
- Every finding has the file, line, source and sink.
- Fixes keep the feature working.
- No eval or document.write remains.
Pitfalls:
- Writing a homemade sanitizer with a regex.
- Escaping once and then decoding before insertion.
- Trusting data because it came from your own storage.
Verify:
- [ ] No innerHTML built from variables.
- [ ] No eval, new Function or document.write.
- [ ] Links from data are protocol checked.
- [ ] No inline handlers.
Output: Fixed scripts and markup plus a findings list (severity, location, fix).

examples.input: revise a segurança do meu app de comentários
examples.output: comments rendered with innerHTML: switched to textContent, link URLs checked with new URL, onclick attributes removed
